A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research despite changed titles and terminology. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original training, finetuning, robustness, transfer-learning and downstream-task results, including repeated-run results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds comparator evaluations, ablations, BERT/GLUE results and CLIP-pretraining results.

M1.justification: The original classification procedure, shared network and averaged supervised/self-distillation losses remain unchanged under renaming. Appendix B adds a CLIP adaptation that distills the main model's image-text similarity matrix into a sub-model receiving masked images, extending the procedure beyond classifier-output distillation.

E1.justification: v2 adds eight GLUE tasks with BERT and CLIP pretraining on CC3M, CC12M and RedCaps, followed by zero-shot ImageNet evaluation. These extend coverage to language and multimodal learning. CLIP image-classification finetuning already existed in v1; the original vision datasets and downstream evaluations remain.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 8–9 add DataAugment, GradAug and CoSub comparisons under DeiT-III training and MAE finetuning. CoSub was previously discussed as Co-sub but not evaluated as a comparator. Tables 2, 4 and 6 also add extensive reported comparisons with pretraining, CLIP-based and self-distillation methods.

E3.justification: New protocols include BERT-base/large with 15% token masking and CLIP ViT-B/32 training with batch size 1,024, 128M seen samples and zero-shot evaluation. Table 8 introduces augmentation comparisons with GradAug trained for 200 epochs versus 400 for other methods. Existing image-classification recipe settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.5 tests removing the KD loss, expands masking-ratio sensitivity to include 0%, 40% and 60%, and introduces a supervised/KD loss-weight sweep. These directly examine components and hyperparameters beyond v1's analyses. Existing convergence, gradient, regularization and robustness analyses are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report three independent runs with different seeds and identical mean/standard-deviation results for regularization, method variants and transfer learning. v1 Tables A.1–A.4 correspond to v2 Tables A.9–A.12. No additional uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Matched original benchmark scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial comparator, ablation and domain results. Examples include BERT-base GLUE averages of 80.9 without versus 81.6 with MaskSub, and CLIP zero-shot accuracies of 33.5 for baseline, 29.8 for masking and 37.6 for MaskSub. Table 10 adds an incorrect Cars gain of +1.3; 92.2 minus 80.9 equals 11.3.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3) preserve the original cross-entropy and self-distillation formulation, with drop-probability notation replaced by masking-ratio notation. Neither version contains additional theorems, proofs or substantive formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion refocus the contribution from general additional drop-based regularization through AugSub to enabling strong masking through MaskSub. Dropout and drop-path remain as extensions, and the central claims of stable convergence and improvements across image-training recipes persist.

C2.justification: v1 identifies applicability beyond visual recognition as untested; v2 interprets its GLUE and CLIP experiments as supporting language and multimodal applicability. Appendix A.1 also attributes worse extended MAE finetuning to overfitting. The adaptive-difficulty explanation and qualifications concerning CIFAR and CLIP finetuning remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds HuggingFace and OpenCLIP implementation references, token-masking instructions, and CLIP hardware, batch-size and sample-budget details. Existing recipe tables and the main code link remain. v2 removes explicit dropout insertion locations and the parameter/FLOP columns from architecture comparison tables.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against self-supervised pretraining, CLIP-based training and self-distillation, adding works such as GradAug, MixSKD, BERT and GLUE. It newly argues that most previous self-distillation methods are incompatible with strong training recipes. Several general augmentation references, including Mixup, CutMix and AutoAugment, disappear.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten around masking. Analysis and variant subsections change order, experiments are reorganized, and the appendix gains thematic subsections. AugMask, AugDrop and AugPath are renamed MaskSub, DropSub and PathSub throughout.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns. Figure 1 is redrawn with explicit masking and stop-gradient connections, removing its accuracy panel. Numerous tables are added, simplified, reordered or relocated to the appendix; Figures 2–3 retain their analyses with revised labels and placement.

improvement.justification: Direct competitor/cost comparisons in Tables 8–9 and KD/loss-weight ablations in Tables A.6–A.8 address important gaps in v1's comparative and component validation. GLUE and CLIP experiments also address its acknowledged scope limitation. These substantially strengthen empirical support. New reporting weaknesses remain: Table 10 has an incorrect Cars delta, and the '1/6 training costs' wording does not match Table 9's total costs of 8.6 versus 23.4 GPU days. These localized problems do not outweigh the stronger validation.
